title: ocbar — your work VPN, under your control
description: An open-source Cisco Secure Client alternative for macOS: choose routes and DNS, use SOCKS and a custom CSD wrapper, and share ready-to-use profiles. Built on OpenConnect.
eyebrow: An open-source alternative to Cisco Secure Client
hero_description: Connect to an AnyConnect-compatible gateway. Choose which traffic uses the VPN, set DNS for work domains, and share a configured profile with colleagues. All from your Mac menu bar.
hero_note: Free & open source · Built locally with Homebrew
menu_alt: Real ocbar interface with a connected demo profile, traffic chart, network switches and DNS zones
profile_alt: Real ocbar profile settings with gateway, networks and DNS configuration
routes_title:
Work goes through.
The rest stays yours.
routes_description: Define networks in your profile and toggle their routes in the menu. Routes sent by the gateway do not automatically become your local routing selection. Everything else keeps its usual path.
routes_detail: Need a moment off the work network? Pause removes ocbar’s routes and DNS zones while keeping the session alive. Resume without another sign-in while that session remains valid.
demo_summary: 2 example networks selected. Try the switches. This does not change your connection.
app_description: See speed and traffic, toggle networks and DNS, and open diagnostics and logs. Your settings are available right in the app.
sso_description: SAML sign-in in a WebKit window, with optional form autofill and TOTP. A valid saved sign-in session can keep the window out of your way.
resume_description: The supervisor reconnects after sleep, network changes and dropped links. If your login expires, the app asks you to sign in.
secrets_description: Use macOS Keychain, KeePassXC or your own command. Profiles hold references to credentials, not the credentials themselves.
install_title:
A few commands.
Then, the menu bar.
install_description: ocbar builds from source on your Mac through Homebrew. After installation, the setup wizard helps you add your gateway and sign in.
step1_note: The tap is a third-party source. Review it before granting trust. Homebrew compiles the app locally.
step2_title: Set up the helper and open ocbar
step2_note: Tunnel mode needs the privileged helper. The first command asks for your Mac administrator password in Terminal.
step3_note: Follow the setup wizard: enter your gateway and group, add the networks and DNS zones you need, then sign in. Ask your VPN administrator for these settings if needed.
faq1_a: No. ocbar is a client for a VPN gateway you already have access to, such as your company’s AnyConnect-compatible gateway. It does not provide VPN servers or an anonymity service.
faq2_q: Will it work with my gateway and Mac?
faq2_a: The author uses it daily on macOS 26 with Apple Silicon, an AnyConnect gateway and Keycloak SSO. macOS 13–25 and Intel Macs are expected to work but are not verified. Gateway policies and sign-in flows vary; compatibility with every deployment is not guaranteed.
faq3_q: Why is there no one-click download?
faq3_a: The app is currently distributed as a Homebrew source build, not a signed and notarized download. You need Command Line Tools; the full Xcode app is not required. Update with brew upgrade ocbar. If the helper changes, run sudo ocbar install again.
faq4_q: Can I use it without changing system routes?
faq4_a: Yes. The optional SOCKS proxy mode uses OpenConnect with ocproxy, without root, system routes or DNS changes. Install ocproxy separately and configure apps to use the local proxy. IPv6 routes inside tunnel mode are not currently supported.
faq5_q: Who maintains it, and what data does it collect?
faq5_a: ocbar is a single-author project by Valery Ignatkovich, released under the MIT license. The app has no analytics, crash reporting or automatic update checks. It talks to your gateway and identity provider and keeps local logs. The source and security model are available on GitHub.
closing_title:
Built by someone who uses it.
Open to everyone who does.
closing_description: ocbar grew out of everyday work with a VPN. The code is open under MIT: inspect it, adapt it, share profiles with your team and contribute improvements.
byline: Made by Valery Ignatkovich · MIT license
disclaimer: Not affiliated with Cisco. AnyConnect describes protocol compatibility.
compatibility: Verified by the author: macOS 26 on Apple Silicon, AnyConnect + Keycloak SSO. macOS 13–25 and Intel are not yet verified.
system_body: Tunnel mode installs a root-owned helper and OpenConnect copy, a background reconnect agent, and a sudoers rule. Members of the Mac’s admin group can run this helper without entering a password each time. The menu bar app itself runs without root privileges.
remove_body: Run these commands in order: first stop the connection and remove the helper, its passwordless rule and background agents; then remove the Homebrew package.
remove_note: Profiles, logs, saved sign-in data and Keychain entries remain. The installation guide explains what is left and where to find full cleanup instructions.
control_intro: For people who need access to a work network and want to configure their own client. Routes, domains, connection mode and diagnostics are in your hands.
traffic_body: Send selected work networks through the tunnel. Choose them in your profile and change them while connected, without editing the server’s VPN policy.
dns_body: Assign a specific DNS server or the gateway’s DNS to a domain. ocbar adds rules for selected zones without replacing DNS for the whole internet.
coexist_body: A work tunnel can coexist with a personal VPN. Keep networks and DNS zones separate between clients. ocbar manages one connection of its own; overlapping routes can conflict.
csd_body: Set a custom HostScan script in your profile. ocbar runs it as your user before SSO. On a compatible gateway, this does not require Cisco Secure Client; the gateway still decides whether to accept the report.
proxy_body: Use SOCKS mode with ocproxy for a browser, Git or one command. With SystemProxy = off, it needs no root helper, system routes or system DNS changes.
logs_body: See speed, traffic, active routes, DNS and local logs in the app. Opening ocbar diagnostics does not require permission from your VPN administrator.
compare_summary: How does this differ from Cisco Secure Client?
compare_body: In Cisco Secure Client, VPN policy configures split tunneling and split DNS; Cisco also provides diagnostics. In ocbar, your profile defines local routes and DNS. You control the client settings, while the gateway still controls resource access and sign-in requirements.
share_title:
Set it up once.
Share it with the team.
share_description: Save every new teammate from rediscovering the gateway, networks, DNS and SSO form. Put the working configuration in one .ocbar file. They import it, set their own account details, and sign in.
share_step1_body: Check the networks, DNS and sign-in form rules with your own connection.
share_step2_body: Export combines connection settings and SSO form rules into one portable profile.
share_step3_body: After importing, they use their own account and credentials to access the work network.
share_note: Passwords and TOTP secrets in your credential store are not exported. Review the username, local paths and custom commands before sharing; teammates must configure their own credential sources.
